appendix_c_entries.exact_appendix_entry: OpenAI. *A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity*. 2026. [Full-text edition](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/4eaee875/preprints/A-Nearly-Quartic-Separation-Between-Randomized-and-Quantum-Query-Complexity-October-5-2026/quartic-query-separation.pdf). Preprint dated 5 October 2026. Mathematical target throughout this record. The retained reviewed PDF has SHA-256 a99f1c38d086a33591b6204ae3957fe3f25c8f31d97c48087325a18fd66daf3e.

Harry Buhrman and Ronald de Wolf. *Complexity Measures and Decision Tree Complexity: A Survey*. 2002. Theoretical Computer Science. 21–43. [Full-text edition](https://homepages.cwi.nl/~rdewolf/publ/qc/dectree.pdf). Author PDF dated 10 October 2002; supplied PDF SHA-256 7002019660c498b652611acf5cdbe264ea9c4a139f8f4da6e82e12822e5d9122. Sections 3.1–3.3, printed pages 5–8, supply the model conventions. Section 3.2 explicitly allows biased coins, takes maximum supported depth, and uses inclusive success at least 2/3. Section 3.3 uses a fixed sequence of input-independent gates and bit queries. Standard exposition, not a proof of the new separation.

Ronald de Wolf. *Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes*. 2026. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.09415v6). Version 6, 27 August 2026. Supplied source archive SHA-256 2ffd080924542b6de1409a1dbd73efcb85e99bc0d3cc2daac5e3eeba84ef2535. Measurement: Section 1.2.2, printed pages 4–6, and Section 2.1.2, pages 14–15. Oracle and phase query: Section 2.4, printed pages 17–18, especially printed footnote 7; Chapter 2, Exercise 10 distinguishes controlled and uncontrolled phase queries. Section 2.3 is Quantum parallelism; the earlier Section 2.3/footnote 17 locator is corrected. Official author PDF independently consulted at https://homepages.cwi.nl/~rdewolf/qcnotes.pdf.

Robert Beals and Harry Buhrman and Richard Cleve and Michele Mosca and Ronald de Wolf. *Quantum Lower Bounds by Polynomials*. 1998. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9802049v3). Conference/arXiv-era version, separately identified from the journal manuscript. The supplied PDF has SHA-256 afec116657493976b70df7dcb8b174c8c0be55a9337d9e035afd5f1fc4d9cd4c. Section 3.2, PDF page 4, defines classical randomized cost using expected queries on a worst-case input; the paragraph following Proposition 6.4, PDF page 9, uses that convention for parity. The arXiv v3 metadata dates it 30 September 1998; no byte identity with a newly downloaded arXiv PDF is asserted. Author-hosted conference PDF also consulted: https://homepages.cwi.nl/~rdewolf/publ/qc/focs98.pdf.

Robert Beals and Harry Buhrman and Richard Cleve and Michele Mosca and Ronald de Wolf. *Quantum Lower Bounds by Polynomials*. 2001. Journal of the ACM. 778–797. [Full-text edition](https://homepages.cwi.nl/~rdewolf/publ/qc/polynomials.pdf). Added external comparison, accessed 2 November 2026. Author-hosted journal manuscript, Section 3.2 printed page 7, uses worst-case randomized query cost; Proposition 6.4 and adjoining paragraph, printed page 17, give quantum parity cost ceil(N/2) and classical bounded-error cost N. The assessment is confined to these passages and version identity. This journal edition uses worst-case query cost, whereas the older conference version uses expected cost.

Aaronson, Scott and Ben-David, Shalev and Kothari, Robin and Rao, Shravas and Tal, Avishay. *Degree vs. Approximate Degree and Quantum Implications of Huang's Sensitivity Theorem*. 2020. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.12629v1). Version 1, 23 October 2020. Theorem 1: pp. 1 and 6–7; Theorem 2 and its deduction: p. 2; Definition 7: p. 6; Lemma 9: p. 8; Conjecture 2: p. 20. Locators refer to the original PDF, not flattened extraction numbering.

Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis. *Forrelation: A Problem That Optimally Separates Quantum from Classical Computing*. 2018. SIAM Journal on Computing. 982–1038. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.5729v1). Mathematical locators refer to the inspected arXiv v1, 21 November 2014, not journal pagination: Section 1.1.3, p. 4; Section 3.2, Figure 1 and Proposition 6, pp. 13–14. Projection probability Phi squared and the separate interference probability (1+Phi)/2 must be distinguished. Journal metadata is supplied for attribution.

Nikhil Bansal and Makrand Sinha. *$k$-Forrelation Optimally Separates Quantum and Classical Query Complexity*. 2021. Proceedings of the 53rd Annual ACM SIGACT Symposium on Theory of Computing. 1303–1316. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.07003v3). Full-version mathematical locators refer to arXiv v3, 17 November 2020: Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4, p. 4; Theorems 3.1–3.4, pp. 16–17; Corollary 3.5, p. 18; Lemma 4.3, p. 19; Section 5.4, p. 38. In supplied v3 main.tex, the disputed comparison is physical line 1181; line 1184 is the later threshold.

Uma Girish and Avishay Tal and Kewen Wu. *Fourier Growth of Parity Decision Trees*. 2021. 36th Computational Complexity Conference (CCC 2021). 39:1–39:36. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.11604v2). Mathematical locators use arXiv v2, 13 May 2021: Section 1.3, pp. 6–8, and Lemma 1.9, p. 8. In the CCC 2021 version the corresponding result is Lemma 9, p. 39:8.

Alexander A. Sherstov and Andrey A. Storozhenko and Pei Wu. *An Optimal Separation of Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity*. 2023. SIAM Journal on Computing. 525–567. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10223v4). Locators refer to arXiv v4, 29 January 2023: PDF Corollaries 4.14–4.15, p. 35; the real-valued proof continues p. 36. The HTML conversion calls these Corollaries 4.12–4.13. The absolute Fourier constant is unspecified.

Avishay Tal. *Towards Optimal Separations between Quantum and Randomized Query Complexities*. 2019. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.12561v1). Version 1, 29 December 2019; published at FOCS 2020. Context only: Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3, p. 13; Definition 5.5 and Lemma 5.7, p. 14.

Aaronson, Scott and Ben-David, Shalev and Kothari, Robin. *Separations in Query Complexity Using Cheat Sheets*. 2016. Proceedings of the 48th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing. 863–876. [Full-text edition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.01937v2). Edition inspected: arXiv v2, 9 July 2019. Printed Section 6.1, Definitions 14–15, pp. 20–21; Section 6.2, Lemma 17, p. 22. These appear as Definitions 10–11 and Lemma 13 in the supplied environment-numbered Markdown extraction. Historical antecedent and algorithmic comparison; no theorem transfer to this multi-column construction.

Ambainis, Andris and Balodis, Kaspars and Belovs, Aleksandrs and Lee, Troy and Santha, Miklos and Smotrovs, Juris. *Separations in Query Complexity Based on Pointer Functions*. 2015. [Full-text edition](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.04719v3). Edition inspected: arXiv v3, 26 October 2015. Section 1.3, pp. 5–6; final paragraph of Use of a balanced tree, p. 6, discusses direct pointers and immediately gives the exponential-alphabet qualification. Historical comparison, not an imported bit-query theorem.

Brassard, Gilles and Høyer, Peter and Mosca, Michele and Tapp, Alain. *Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation*. 2000. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0005055v1). Inspected arXiv v1. Section 2, Lemma 1, printed pages 5–6, and equation (8), page 7: amplification geometry and successful component. Theorem 3, pages 8–9: expected-time unknown-success search, not the all-branch cap. Theorem 12, page 19, is amplitude estimation. Published version: Contemporary Mathematics 305 (2002), pages 53–74; locators in this record refer to v1.

Boyer, Michel and Brassard, Gilles and Høyer, Peter and Tapp, Alain. *Tight Bounds on Quantum Searching*. 1996. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9605034v1). Inspected arXiv v1. Section 4, Lemma 2, printed page 3: exact average for a random number of Grover iterations. Theorem 3 and subsequent timeout discussion, page 4: unknown-number expected-time search. The fixed capped construction is proved separately in §5.1. Journal version: Fortschritte der Physik 46 (1998); its pagination is not used for these locators.

Dürr, Christoph and Høyer, Peter. *A Quantum Algorithm for Finding the Minimum*. 1999. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9607014v2). Inspected revised arXiv v2; original preprint July 1996. Theorem 1 and Lemmas 1–2, pages 1–2. Historical comparison only: ordered values and rank improvement do not supply a proof for arbitrary probabilistic comparisons.

Høyer, Peter and Mosca, Michele and de Wolf, Ronald. *Quantum Search on Bounded-Error Inputs*. 2003. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0304052v2). Inspected arXiv v2. Section 1, pages 1–3: uniform bounded-error access to fixed Boolean predicates. Section 3, pages 4–7: search construction. Section 4: AND–OR applications. Section 5, pages 8–9: imperfect-verifier generalization. Hypothesis comparison only; arbitrary loser comparisons need not satisfy the fixed-predicate correctness guarantee. Published in ICALP 2003, LNCS 2719, pages 291–299; locators here use v2.

Ambainis, Andris and Iraids, Jānis and Kokainis, Mārtiņš. *Near-Optimal Separations of Certificate Complexity from Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity*. 2026. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11664v2). arXiv v2. Recent comparison-based separation of certificate complexity identified by the preprint's §1.1; cited as an antecedent for comparison and certificate checking, with no theorem imported as a premise.

Ben-David, Shalev and Kothari, Robin. *Randomized Query Complexity Can Beat Certificate Complexity*. 2026. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15063v1). Inspected arXiv v1, Section 3, Lemma 5, pages 3–5. Antecedent for candidate generation, tournament comparison and certificate checking; no theorem from this source is imported as a premise of the fractional-weight proof.

Mande, Nikhil S. and Paraashar, Manaswi and Saurabh, Nitin. *Randomized and Quantum Query Complexities of Finding a King in a Tournament*. 2023. 43rd IARCS Annual Conference on Foundations of Software Technology and Theoretical Computer Science (FSTTCS 2023). 30:1–30:19. [Published edition](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.FSTTCS.2023.30). Inspected published edition. Theorem 19, Section 4, pages 30:11–30:13, including the nearby proof and Algorithm 4. Exact direction queries to a fixed tournament; contextual comparison only. The baseline's Theorem 4.4 locator does not match this edition.

Drucker, Andrew. *Improved Direct Product Theorems for Randomized Query Complexity*. 2012. Computational Complexity. 197–244. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.0644v2). Assessed arXiv version 2, 9 May 2014, and supplied pinned TeX. All locators use arXiv printed pagination: Section 1.3, pp. 6–7; Lemmas 3.1–3.2, pp. 11–12; fair specialization at the end of Section 3, p. 13. Relevant passages of the earlier supplied PDF agree; complete edition identity was not established

Shaltiel, Ronen. *Towards Proving Strong Direct Product Theorems*. 2001. [Report page](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2001/009/). Assessed ECCC report: Section 1.1, p. 1, definitions of success/advantage and footnotes 1–2; Section 5, Definition 4 and Theorem 5, printed p. 11, and Lemma 7, p. 12. These are PDF pages 12–13. Later journal publication: Computational Complexity 12(1–2):1–22 (2003); journal-edition theorem numbering not assessed

Huang, Hao. *Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture*. 2019. Annals of Mathematics. 949–955. [Full-text edition](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v190-n3-p06-s.pdf). Published edition inspected at Lemma 2.2, p. 952, and the proof and spectral remark for Theorem 1.1, p. 953. The supplied six-page source is instead arXiv:1907.00847v2; its corresponding locators are pp. 4–5.

Midrijānis, Gatis. *Exact quantum query complexity for total Boolean functions*. 2004. [Version record](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0403168v2). Version 2, 27 March 2004. Lemma 3, p. 3; proof of Theorem 4, pp. 3–4, especially its final paragraph for D(f) <= deg(f) bs(f). Theorem 5 concerns exact, not bounded-error, quantum query complexity.

Høyer, Peter and Lee, Troy and Špalek, Robert. *Negative weights make adversaries stronger*. 2007. [Full-text edition](https://www.ucw.cz/~robert/papers/madv.pdf). The inspected 29-page author PDF: Definition 1 and Theorem 1, printed p. 3. Version-2 metadata is dated 24 April 2007; byte identity of the author PDF and arXiv PDF was not established. Theorem 1 attributes the nonnegative spectral bound, including denominator two, to Barnum–Saks–Szegedy. Related conference publication: STOC 2007, pp. 526–535, DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250867.

Špalek, Robert and Szegedy, Mario. *All Quantum Adversary Methods are Equivalent*. 2006. Theory of Computing. 1–18. [Full-text edition](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v002a001/v002a001.pdf). Publisher edition. Oracle convention: Section 2.1, p. 4; operator norm: Section 2.4, p. 5; Theorem 3.1 and equation (3.1): p. 6; closing proof: p. 14. The printed error prefactor lacks a factor 1/2 under those conventions; the exact two-bit parity witness checks this local discrepancy without disputing the nonnegative-adversary equivalences.

Barnum, Howard and Saks, Michael and Szegedy, Mario. *Quantum query complexity and semi-definite programming*. 2003. Proceedings of the 18th IEEE Annual Conference on Computational Complexity. 179–193. [Publication metadata](https://doi.org/10.1109/CCC.2003.1214419). The proceedings title and DOI are confirmed by the [Rutgers institutional record](https://www.researchwithrutgers.org/en/publications/quantum-query-complexity-and-semi-definite-programming/). The attribution of the adversary theorem follows Høyer–Lee–Špalek Theorem 1 and Špalek–Szegedy reference 7. Original full text was not supplied or independently inspected in this review.

complexitylib contributors. *complexitylib: pinned Lean source dependency*. [Full-text edition](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/tree/62ca5c21461b2482e8bd12b7cb9b4937d887a33a). Revision read from the supplied lake-manifest.json and DEPENDENCY_SOURCES.json. Exact proof-source and run evidence are recorded separately in correspondence.json; a source citation alone does not assert successful compilation. No repository commit date or individual author list is inferred.

Mika Göös, Toniann Pitassi and Thomas Watson. *Deterministic communication vs. Partition number*. SIAM Journal on Computing (2018), DOI [10.1137/16M1059369](https://doi.org/10.1137/16M1059369). The retained baseline assessment uses [ECCC TR15-050](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2015/050/), revision text dated 5 September 2017, Theorem 5 and §2.1, pp. 3–5. Historical construction antecedent; this integration does not claim a fresh full reading.
